claims.text: The proposed framework includes three modules: Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG), Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA), and Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG).
claims.poster_quote: We propose a three-module framework: 1) Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG) constructs an organ-level graph using pre-trained organ segmentations and clinical prior knowledge to model invasion patterns between primary sites and surrounding organs. 2) Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) performs fine-grained alignment by using each organ node as a query over the radiology report to selectively aggregate relevant textual evidence, enhancing organ features while preserving anatomical topology. 3) Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG) uses a large language model to extract explicit invasion statements from the report and injects them as a text node connected only to primary sites and invaded organs, refining the graph without discarding anatomy-based risk connections.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our framework comprises three key components: an Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG), an Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) module, and a Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG) module.
claims.reason: Section III Methods, page 4: The paper explicitly lists the three modules included in the framework.
